about: Who we are

Leaflegal is a free introduction service that helps people and businesses find a regulated law firm for their matter. It is a trading name of Vertical Brands Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales with company number 14254961. Our registered office is at 20-22 Wenlock Road, London, N1 7GU.

Our team runs the website, checks enquiries and works with the firms we introduce people to. We are not lawyers and we are not a law firm. We do not give legal advice or immigration advice, and we are not regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority. What we do is make introductions carefully and explain plainly how the process works.

We focus on eight areas of law. Six of them are for matters in England and Wales. Those are conveyancing, lease extensions, family law, motoring offences, licensing and business debt recovery. The other two cover the whole of the UK. They are trademarks and related IP, because there is one UK trademark register, and introductions to regulated immigration advisers.

Our aim is simple. When someone needs a lawyer, we want the first step to be quick, clear and free of pressure. That means one short form, one regulated firm that handles that kind of matter, and an honest explanation of how we are paid.

Why we exist

Legal problems rarely arrive at a convenient time. A house sale falls behind schedule. A relationship ends. A letter arrives from the court or the police. A customer stops paying. In each case there is often a deadline, and the person dealing with it is already under strain.

Finding the right lawyer in that moment can be surprisingly hard. Most people do not know many solicitors, and the ones they know may not do the right kind of work. Searching online brings up a long list of names with little to tell them apart. Calling round takes time, and it often means explaining the same story again and again to people who then say they cannot help.

about.h3: What we set out to change

about: We wanted to remove that first round of searching. Instead of you finding the firm, you tell us about your matter once, and we introduce a firm that handles that kind of work. The firm calls you knowing the basics, so the conversation starts in the right place.

We also wanted to be honest about it. Many websites that offer to find you a lawyer are not clear about who runs them, how they are paid or how many firms receive your details. We think people deserve to know exactly who they are dealing with, so we explain all of that on our website in plain words.

We chose to focus on a small number of areas where people often need a specialist and where a quick introduction can make a real difference. Keeping our focus narrow means we understand the questions to ask and the firms we work with handle that work every day. It also means we do not pretend to help with things we cannot.

about.h3: What a good introduction looks like

about: For us, a good introduction is one where the firm calls promptly, already understands the outline of the matter, explains clearly what it can do and what it will cost, and leaves the decision with you. It is not one where you feel rushed or chased. We design the form, the checks and our arrangements with firms around that idea.

We also know that not every enquiry will lead to someone instructing a firm. Some people just want to understand where they stand. Some decide to handle things themselves, or find that the matter resolves on its own. That is fine. Speaking to a regulated firm early can still help people make better decisions, whatever they choose to do next.

We write for people who have never dealt with a solicitor before as much as for those who have. That is why our pages use plain words, short sentences and as little jargon as possible. When a legal term cannot be avoided, we try to explain it. Our guides also include a section of common legal terms in plain English, so you can follow what your lawyer is saying.
What we do
Our work happens mostly behind the scenes. Here is what we actually do when you use Leaflegal.

The questions on the form are designed for each area of law. They are the questions a firm's intake team would usually ask first. That way the firm can see quickly what kind of matter it is, how urgent it is and where you are.

We check that each enquiry is complete, that it falls within the areas we cover and that the contact details work. We also check that you have given your consent to be introduced. This helps make sure firms only receive enquiries they can actually help with, and that people only hear from a firm when they have asked to.

We pass each enquiry to one regulated firm that handles that type of matter and covers your area. For immigration, it goes to a regulated immigration adviser. We send the firm your answers, your contact details and a record of your consent.

Our pages explain in general terms how different kinds of matters usually work in England and Wales, what tends to affect cost and time, and what to have ready. They are not legal advice, but they can help you feel more prepared when you speak to a lawyer.

If something goes wrong with an introduction, or if a firm does not treat someone well, we want to know. We use that feedback to improve the service and to decide which firms we continue to work with.

We keep a record of each enquiry, the consent given and the firm it was introduced to. That lets us answer questions, deal with complaints and show that introductions were made properly. Our privacy policy explains how long we keep these records and how you can ask to see them.

about.h3: We keep the website up to date

about: Legal procedures, court fees, government forms and official guidance change from time to time. We review our pages regularly and update them when something important changes. Where figures change often, such as fees and tax rates, we do not quote them and instead point you to GOV.UK or the firm, so you always get the current position from the right source.
What we are not
It matters to us that you know exactly who you are dealing with, so here is a plain list of what Leaflegal is not.

about.h3: Why we do not give advice

about: Giving legal advice is a skilled job, and in some areas, such as immigration, it is a criminal offence for anyone who is not regulated to give it. Our role is to make the introduction. The regulated firm we introduce you to is the right place for advice about your situation, because it can look at all the details and it is accountable to its regulator for what it tells you.

Leaflegal is responsible for the introduction itself, for how we handle your information and for the information on our website. The firm is responsible for the advice it gives, the work it does, the fees it charges and how it treats you as a client. If you have a complaint about the introduction, it comes to us. If you have a complaint about the legal service, it goes to the firm first.

Our pages explain in general terms how things usually work in England and Wales, and for immigration, how working with a regulated adviser usually goes. We try hard to keep them accurate and up to date. Laws, fees and procedures do change, though, and general information can never take account of your own circumstances. Always check the position with a regulated firm before you act.

about.h3: Not a substitute for the firm

about: We sometimes hear from people who want us to tell them whether they have a good case, whether a quote is fair or what will happen at a hearing. We understand why, but those are questions only a regulated lawyer who knows the facts can answer properly. We will always point you back to the firm, or to another regulated adviser, rather than guess.
The firms we work with

We introduce people to independent firms that are regulated for the work they do. For most areas that means firms of solicitors regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority. For conveyancing it can also mean firms regulated by the Council for Licensed Conveyancers. For immigration it means solicitors or advisers who are regulated to give immigration advice, such as those registered with the Immigration Advice Authority.

Firms that want to receive introductions talk to our team first and agree in writing how the arrangement works. They choose the areas of law, types of matter and locations they handle. That helps us introduce each enquiry to a firm that does that kind of work.

To treat people's information with care

about: If we hear that a firm has not treated people fairly, we take it seriously. We look into what happened and may stop introducing people to that firm. We cannot investigate a firm's legal work, which is a matter for the firm's own complaints procedure and its regulator, but we can and do decide who we work with.

The firms we introduce are not part of Leaflegal and we are not part of them. Each firm has its own regulator, its own professional indemnity insurance and its own complaints procedure. That independence is important. It means the firm owes its professional duties to you as its client, not to us.

The firms we work with are based in different parts of England and Wales, and for immigration across the UK. For many matters the firm does not need to be close to you, because most work is done by phone, email and post. Where local knowledge matters, such as a hearing at your local court or an application to your local council, we take that into account.
How we are paid

Leaflegal is free for people and businesses to use. We are paid by the firm we introduce you to. Each firm pays us an agreed fee for the introductions we send. That income covers the cost of running the website, our advertising and the checks we carry out on enquiries.

The fee the firm pays us does not change what the firm charges you. The firm sets its own prices and will explain them before any work starts. Solicitors must tell you in writing about any fee they pay for an introduction, and the fee must not affect the advice they give you.

We introduce each enquiry based on the type of matter and where you are, not on which firm pays us the most. We do not rank firms for you or claim that one firm is better than another. You are always free to speak to other firms and to choose who you instruct.
You can read more on our how we make money page.

about.h3: Why the firm pays rather than you

about: Firms spend money on finding new clients in many ways, such as advertising, directories and websites. Paying for an introduction is one of those ways. Because the firm pays, we can keep the service free for you, and you can find out whether a firm is right for you without spending anything.
faqs: About us
Who owns Leaflegal?

Leaflegal is a trading name of Vertical Brands Ltd, a private company registered in England and Wales with company number 14254961. Our registered office is at 20-22 Wenlock Road, London, N1 7GU. Our full company details, including our VAT number, are shown on this page and in the footer of every page.
Is Leaflegal a law firm?

No. Leaflegal is an introduction service. We are not a law firm, we do not employ solicitors to advise the public and we are not regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority. The firms we introduce people to are independent and regulated, and they give the advice.
Where is Leaflegal based?

Our registered office is in London. Most of our work is done online, and the firms we introduce people to are spread across England and Wales. For immigration we introduce people across the whole of the UK to regulated advisers.
Who do you help?

People and businesses looking for paid help from a lawyer in conveyancing, lease extensions, family law, motoring offences, licensing or business debt recovery in England and Wales. We also introduce individuals, families and employers anywhere in the UK to regulated immigration advisers.
What areas of law do you cover?

Eight. Conveyancing, lease extensions, family law, motoring offences, licensing and business debt recovery, all for matters in England and Wales, plus trademarks and related IP and introductions to regulated immigration advisers anywhere in the UK. We do not cover personal injury, clinical negligence, housing disrepair or financial mis-selling claims.
Why don't you cover more areas?

We would rather do a few things well than many things badly. Focusing on eight areas means our questions are right for each one and the firms we work with handle that work every day. Some areas, such as personal injury, are also subject to rules that ban referral fees, so they are not suitable for a service like ours.
Do you work with any charities or advice services?

Leaflegal is a commercial introduction service and is not linked to any charity or free advice service. If you need free help, organisations such as Citizens Advice, local law centres and, for some matters, legal aid providers may be able to assist.
How we work
What does Leaflegal actually do?

We run the website and form, check each enquiry, and introduce it to one regulated firm that handles that type of matter and covers your area. We also publish general guides explaining how different kinds of matters usually work. We do not act for you or give advice about your situation.
Do you speak to me before introducing a firm?

Usually not. The form is designed to give the firm what it needs to start the conversation, so we can introduce you quickly. If something in your enquiry is unclear or looks outside the areas we cover, we may get in touch to check before passing it on.
Do you follow up after the introduction?

Once you are introduced, you deal with the firm directly. We do not manage your matter. We do want to hear from you if the firm did not get in touch, if something about the introduction went wrong or if you were not treated fairly.
Can I speak to someone at Leaflegal?

You can email us at any time and a member of our team will reply. We are not able to discuss the legal side of your matter, because we do not give advice, but we can help with questions about the form, the introduction or your information.
Can I use Leaflegal more than once?

Yes. If you have a new matter later on, or a second matter at the same time, you can fill in the form again. Each enquiry is introduced to a firm that handles that particular type of work, so you may be introduced to a different firm each time.
Do you give advice about which area I need?

We can help you pick the right part of the form if you are unsure, but we do not give legal advice about your matter. If your situation touches more than one area, describe it in your own words and the firm will explain what kind of help fits once it understands the details.
What if my matter is outside your areas?

If your matter is not something we cover, we will not pass it to a firm. The Law Society's Find a Solicitor service lists solicitors by area of law and location, and Citizens Advice can help you understand where to start. GOV.UK can also help you check whether legal aid may be available.
Can Leaflegal give me a quote?

No. We do not set or quote legal fees. The firm we introduce you to will explain its own fees and confirm them in writing before any work starts. If you want to compare, you are free to ask other firms for quotes as well.
Firms
How do you choose which firms to work with?

We work with independent firms that are regulated for the work they do and that handle the areas and locations we cover. Firms agree in writing how the arrangement works. We expect them to contact people promptly, explain fees clearly and be honest when they cannot help.
Are the firms you introduce regulated?

Yes. We only introduce firms that are regulated for the type of work involved, such as solicitors regulated by the SRA, licensed conveyancers regulated by the CLC or regulated immigration advisers. It is still sensible to check for yourself, for example on the SRA register.
Do you recommend one firm over another?

No. We introduce one firm that handles your type of matter and covers your area. We do not rank firms or claim that a particular firm is the best. The choice to instruct the firm, or anyone else, is always yours.
What happens if a firm treats me badly?

Raise it with the firm first, because every regulated firm must have a complaints procedure. Please tell us as well. We take it seriously, and we may stop working with firms that do not treat people fairly. Concerns about a solicitor's conduct can also go to the SRA.
I run a law firm. Can I work with you?

Yes. Our page for law firms explains how firms receive introductions from Leaflegal and how to get in touch with our team. Please do not use the client form for this, as it is only for people and businesses looking for legal help.
Can I check a firm before I speak to it?

Yes, and we encourage it. You can search for a solicitor or firm on the SRA register, look up a licensed conveyancer with the Council for Licensed Conveyancers or check an immigration adviser with their regulator. The firm should also be happy to tell you who regulates it.
Are the firms paid to give me a particular answer?

No. The firm pays us for the introduction, and nobody pays the firm to give you a particular answer. Solicitors must act in their clients' best interests, and the referral fee must not affect the advice they give. If you ever feel a firm is not being straight with you, tell the firm and tell us.
Being open
How does Leaflegal make money?

Leaflegal is free for you. Firms pay us an agreed fee for each introduction we send them. That fee does not change what the firm charges you, and solicitors must tell you about it in writing. Our how we make money page explains this in more detail.
Does the firm that pays most get my enquiry?

No. We introduce each enquiry based on the type of matter and your location. We do not run an auction for your enquiry and we do not recommend a firm because it pays us more. Each enquiry goes to one firm only and is not sold on.
Do you share my details with anyone else?

We share your enquiry with the one firm we introduce you to, and only because you agreed to it. We never share the details of your matter with advertisers or data brokers. Our privacy policy sets out how we use, store and protect your information.
Do you publish reviews or success rates?

No. We do not publish testimonials or claim success rates, because each legal matter is different and outcomes depend on the facts and the work of the firm. If you want to know about a firm, ask it directly about its experience with matters like yours.
How can I complain about Leaflegal?

Email us with complaint in the subject line. Tell us what went wrong and what you would like us to do. We acknowledge complaints within three working days and aim to give a full written response within fifteen working days. Our complaints page has the full process.
Are you regulated by anyone?

Leaflegal is not a law firm, so we are not regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority. As a company we must follow UK law, including data protection law and consumer protection law. The firms we introduce are regulated by their own professional bodies for the legal work they do.
Do firms pay you whether or not I instruct them?

Yes. Firms pay for the introduction itself, not for the outcome. That means we have no reason to push you towards instructing the firm. Whether you go ahead is entirely your decision, and it makes no difference to Leaflegal either way.
Your information
What information do you hold about me?

We hold the answers you gave on the form, your contact details, the record of your consent and which firm we introduced you to. We use that to make the introduction and to deal with any questions or complaints. Our privacy policy explains this in full, including how long we keep it.
Can I see the information you hold?

Yes. You have the right to ask for a copy of the personal information we hold about you. Email us and we will explain how to make the request. You can also ask us to correct anything that is wrong or, in many cases, to delete it.
Who can I contact about my data?

Email us and we will help. If you are not happy with how we have handled your personal information, you can also raise a concern with the Information Commissioner's Office, which is the UK regulator for data protection.
Do you use cookies?

Our website uses cookies that it needs to work. Other cookies, such as those used to measure our adverts, are only used if you accept them, and you can change your choice at any time using the cookie settings link at the bottom of every page. Our cookie policy explains what we use and why.
